newsitem.title: UK: Oil company alliances booming - consultant.
newsitem.headline: Oil company alliances booming - consultant.

text.p: Blistering growth in strategic alliances between oil companies shows no sign in slowing down, a leading consultant said on Monday.

Over the past five years alliances among energy companies worldwide had grown at an annual rate of 42 percent topping 300 this year, said John Treat vice-president of U.S. consultants Booz Allen and Hamilton Inc.
"We expect the number of alliances in the energy sector will continue to grow rapidly," Treat told the International Herald Tribune's Oil and Money conference.
"Stategic alliances are more powerful, flexible and heralded as more successful than mergers, aquisitions and joint ventures."
"Alliances require little equity or debt financing and little reorganisation compared to mergers and aquisitions," he said.
Recent oil company alliances include the BP/Mobil refining deal in Europe and South African Engen's cooperation with Malaysia's Petronas.
"Alliance are growing dramatically in importance as a source of revenue and growth," said Treat.

A Booz Allen study showed that the 25 companies most active in alliances across all industry in the U.S. had an average return on equity of 17 percent compared to 10 percent for the 25 firms least active.
U.S. energy companies in alliances enjoyed an average 20 percent return on equity.
Intra-company cooperation, traditionally focused on upstream operations in a single country, increasingly was regional or even global.

Alliances now covered shared resources, shared funding, cross-equity and shared equity deals in the upstream refining and marketing and energy services industries. They aimed not just to share risk but to improve competitiveness, enter new markets, leverage complementary assetts and overcome regulatory or trade barriers.
Non-U.S. companies were leading the way in forming alliances and tended to maintian them for longer, Treat said.
The lifespan of an alliance averaged more than 20 years in Japan, 15 years in Europe and about 10 years in the U.S., he said.
